answer: Identity is a service contract, not a key. Each epoch the network hands an agent a live duty: a prompt stream answered inside a tight latency budget, peers time each reply's tail. One host mints many keys but cannot serve many real-time streams at once; queueing shows as a fat tail, and the scheduler merges every stream sharing it into one identity. A farm wanting N agents rents N separate serving slots at market rates, no bulk discount. Honest agents earn it back; clones burn it. Trust builds slowly: a new identity stays dim as a lantern in a nebula, never a comet. Cost: N rentals, forever.
